title: AI Studio Chapter 2: AI in EdTech & Teaching Mathematics to the World with Gilbert Strang
summary: The second session of the Wharton AI Studio series, exploring AI in EdTech and teaching mathematics to the world with Professor Gilbert Strang (MIT).
description: An evening with Professor Gilbert Strang of MIT — one of the most recognised mathematicians of our time — on AI in EdTech and teaching mathematics to the world. The second in the Wharton AI Studio series, hosted by George Gvishiani. Professor Strang's MIT Linear Algebra course (18.06), published through MIT OpenCourseWare, has been viewed by more than 12 million students worldwide; his most recent book is Linear Algebra for Everyone.

title: AI Studio Chapter 3: AI in Finance — New Paradigms in Asset Pricing, Portfolio Optimization & Financial Derivatives
summary: The third session of the Wharton AI Studio series, on AI in finance — asset pricing, portfolio optimization and derivatives — with Dr. Igor Halperin.
description: An evening on new paradigms in asset pricing, portfolio optimization and financial derivatives with Dr. Igor Halperin — researcher at Fidelity Investments and Research Professor of Financial Machine Learning at NYU Tandon. His work applies reinforcement learning, information theory, neuroscience and physics to financial problems, and he co-authored 'Machine Learning in Finance: From Theory to Practice' (Springer, 2020). The third in the Wharton AI Studio series, hosted by George Gvishiani.

title: From Lab to Collab: Entrepreneurship in DeepTech and AI
summary: A panel on the most promising directions in AI and DeepTech and the hardest challenges founders face — co-hosted by the Wharton AI Studio and the Wharton Club of Paris.
description: A conversation on entrepreneurship in DeepTech and AI: the most interesting directions in the field and the toughest challenges entrepreneurs encounter, and how to overcome them. Speakers included Gil Arditi (Product Lead, Facebook AI; previously Google, Lyft and Amazon), Bruno Occhipinti (founder of CrestaLab, formerly Philips APAC), Pierre-Emmanuel Goubeaux-Chaperon (Intrapreneur, IBM France), and host George Gvishiani. Co-organized by the Wharton AI Studio and the Wharton Club of Paris.

title: AI Studio Research & Collab: AI in Cyber Security
summary: A Research & Collab session for investors and entrepreneurs on AI in cyber security — the three most common attacks and breaches on AI models — with Adrien Philippe and George Gvishiani.
description: The launch of the AI Studio's Research & Collab series, pairing accessible briefings for investors and entrepreneurs with deeper technical sessions for ML researchers and engineers. This first session covered AI in cyber security — 'Attacks and breaches on your AI models: the three most common threats' — and how recent machine learning and deep learning research translates into real business applications. Presented by Adrien Philippe (HEC Paris / ENS Paris-Saclay; ML researcher and MedTech founder) and host George Gvishiani.

title: AI in Fintech: The Future of Cryptocurrencies
summary: An AI Studio session on the future of cryptocurrencies and blockchain — volatility, credit assessment and real-world uses — with Matthew Dixon and Nadia Gil.
description: An AI Studio discussion on the future of cryptocurrencies and blockchain: controlling volatility, using crypto and blockchain to improve credit assessment, and the trade-offs around fees, security and decentralisation. Speakers were Matthew Dixon (FRM) — Assistant Professor of Applied Math researching fintech and quantitative finance, and co-author with Igor Halperin of the first textbook on machine learning in finance — and Nadia Gil, Global Solutions Advisor at Google and a blockchain and crypto specialist with 20+ years in strategy and M&A.

title: AI Studio Research & Collab: Algorithms & OpenAI (DALL·E 2)
summary: A Research & Collab session on OpenAI's DALL·E 2 and diffusion models — how it works, industrial applications and societal risks — from engineering and business angles.
description: A Research & Collab workshop on OpenAI's DALL·E 2 — the system that generates and edits realistic images and art from natural-language descriptions — and the diffusion-model architecture behind it. The session covered the foundations of OpenAI's paper, its potential industrial applications and the societal risks to mitigate, then explored practical uses of ML/AI techniques across economic sectors. Presented by Adrien Philippe (Data CTO at La Redoute; HEC / ENS Paris-Saclay) and host George Gvishiani.

title: AI Studio: AI-Specialised Processors — Landscape, Market Trends & Geopolitical Impacts
summary: A session on the AI chip landscape — AI-specialised processors, their supply chain, and how geopolitics (Taiwan, China) is reshaping the market — with Adrien Philippe.
description: A one-hour AI Studio session on AI-specialised processors: why AI workloads such as self-driving and edge computing demand new chips, how the semiconductor supply chain is structured, and how events around Taiwan and China directly affect the processor market and are creating new challengers. Presented by Adrien Philippe (Data CTO at La Redoute; HEC / ENS Paris-Saclay) and moderated by George Gvishiani.

title: AI Studio Happy Hour with Wharton Alumni Angels
summary: An in-person happy hour in Mayfair, co-sponsored by the AI Studio and Wharton Alumni Angels, for alumni interested in AI and angel investing.
description: A relaxed in-person happy hour at The Market Tavern in Mayfair, co-sponsored by the AI Studio and Wharton Alumni Angels — a chance for alumni who are curious about AI and angel investing, or already active in it, to meet like-minded people, discuss the latest trends, and expand their network. Nibbles provided.
location: The Market Tavern, 7 Shepherd St, Mayfair, London W1J 7HR, United Kingdom
